body: Seen while implementing inline mode: with the probe app at 60 body lines in a 30-row terminal (inline, Screen:inline has top and bottom tall borders), the frame shows the top border on row 0 and body lines on rows 1-29; the bottom border row is painted over by the overflowing body, and no scrollbar is visible. Python clips the Screen's children to its content region inside the border and scrolls them (overflow-y auto), so the bottom border stays. Not yet checked whether full-screen apps with a bordered, overflowing Screen do the same (likely a general child-clipping gap, not inline-specific). Repro: tests/fixtures/inline_probe with PROBE_LINES=60 under tests/inline_mode.rs inl_004.

body: A pushed screen whose content is taller than the terminal cannot scroll, in full-screen and inline mode. In a 40x20 headless run a 60-line pushed Screen drew a scrollbar, but pagedown left it on lines 1-20. The screen root (ScreenHost in src/screen.rs) has no scroll state, and no wheel or key handling. Python scrolls every Screen (default overflow-y: auto). INL-017 asks that content taller than the frame scrolls inside each screen, so an inline pushed screen taller than the terminal does not meet it until this lands. The developer chose to build this as its own commitment (escalation 2ab7b8e7, answered ok).

subject: Pushed screens scroll like the app's own screen: ScreenHost keeps the shared ScrollHost state, so the mouse wheel and a scrollbar drag move a Screen or ModalScreen as far as its last line, in full-screen and inline mode; its content is clipped inside its border; its scrollbar and tooltip stay unscrolled.

body: Updating a widget from an app handler through App::with_widget_mut, with_widget_mut_as, with_query_one_mut or with_query_one_mut_as does not redraw it when the update keeps the widget's size. with_widget_mut (src/runtime/mod.rs:3334-3376) runs the closure without a WidgetCtx and requests a relayout only when the widget's intrinsic size probes change; it never requests a repaint. Repro (throwaway PTY test, full-screen and inline, with or without a focused Button): the inline probe's on_key_with_app counts an unbound key and updates #status from 'keys:0' to 'keys:1' with with_query_one_mut_as::<Static>; the screen keeps showing keys:0 until another key ('s') forces a relayout, then shows keys:1. Python's Static.update always refreshes the widget (static.py update -> self.refresh(layout=True)). This is the real cause behind focused-button-swallows-unbound-keys: the key does reach the app.

subject: A widget changed through App::with_widget_mut, with_widget_mut_as, with_query_one_mut or with_query_one_mut_as is repainted in the next frame, in full-screen and inline mode, including when an input repaints another widget in the same frame (127c88b6, 6be0d312)

body: A region-scoped full-screen frame composes the whole tree, writes only its dirty regions (FrameBuffer::diff_to_segments_in_regions) and then stores the whole composed buffer as the current frame (present_composed_frame: self.frame = next). A change composed outside the regions is therefore recorded as drawn but never written, and no later frame writes it, not even a full-content one, until those cells change again or the screen is cleared. widget-update-skips-repaint (6be0d312) closed the path for repaints the app queues; any other change that skips invalidation still gets stuck. Keeping the previous cells outside the regions in the stored frame would make later frames write it.
title: Promote frame-keeps-unwritten-cells
